Check whether a roxygen2 file's documented row count matches the data

Source: R/update.R
sd_check_row_count.Rd

A fast, LLM-free diagnostic, symmetric to sd_check_documentation_current() but for ROWS (respondents) instead of variables. Reads the row count recorded in the existing roxygen2 file's @format line (e.g. "A data frame with 200 rows and 17 variables:") and compares it to nrow(x$data).

Usage

sd_check_row_count(x, object_name, file = NULL)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object containing the CURRENT data.

object_name

Name the documented object has, e.g. "survey_data" – the same name used with sd_generate_roxygen().

file

Path to the existing roxygen2 file. Defaults to file.path("R", paste0(object_name, ".R")).

Value

Invisibly, the difference nrow(x$data) - <documented count> (0 when up to date). Called for its printed message.

Details

Unlike new variables, new rows do not require any change to the \describe{} block itself – only the row count in @format needs correcting, which sd_update_row_count() does deterministically. But because sd_document()'s descriptive text (respondent counts, distributions, and so on) is computed from the WHOLE dataset, a change in row count is also a strong signal that that text is now stale and worth regenerating by hand with sd_document() – this function does not attempt to do that automatically.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sd_check_row_count(aineisto, "survey_data")
} # }
